title: Batch/Cache Rollout Safety: rollback criteria, smoke metrics & dashboarding
creator: Anita Kumar
description:
Goal: Build an experiment and automated safety layer for applying batching and KV-cache configuration changes with clear rollback triggers and a set of smoke metrics + dashboards for rapid diagnosis. This ticket covers the experiment instrumentation, hypothesis & metric definitions, rollout policy automation, and a dashboard/alert pack for on-call and product owners.

Scope:
- Define per-request and per-tenant telemetry to compare baseline vs variant for batching/cache parameter changes (batch size caps, aggregation window, prefix-KV ttl, cache hot-shard policies).
- Implement canary rollout automation with stepwise percentages and automated rollback.
- Create an experiment analysis pipeline (cohort tagging, aggregation windows, statistical tests, and a dashboard template).
- Add alerts in Console for safety thresholds and integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.

Why different from prior experiments: previous tickets focused on adaptive batching logic and AB test infra. This work formalizes safety criteria (smoke metrics + decision rules) and delivers a reusable dashboard + automation for fast rollback and postmortem analysis.

Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use short-window smoke metrics (1h/6h) for automated rollback to reduce blast radius vs waiting for full statistical significance. We'll use short-window conservative thresholds for auto-rollback and longer-window stat tests for final evaluation.
- Prioritize token cost and p95 latency as primary safety signals; retain quality checks via a small synthetic eval set (latency-insensitive) rather than full-scale human eval during canary.
- Conservative rollouts: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over a minimum duration per step (configurable), with automatic pause/rollback on violations.

Telemetry to collect (per request):
- request_id, tenant_id, model_id, model_variant, route, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, queue_ms, serve_ms, status_code, error_flag, cache_hit_flag, cache_ttl_bucket, batch_size.
- tag requests with experiment_key and cohort (control/variant) for grouping.

Primary smoke metrics (short-window):
- Unit cost delta: relative change in billed tokens-compute units per request aggregated (1h window). Auto-rollback if variant increases unit cost by >= 8% over baseline for two consecutive 1h windows.
- Latency p95: absolute increase > 20ms OR relative increase > 10% for two consecutive 1h windows -> rollback.
- Error rate: absolute increase > 0.1 percentage points (e.g., 0.2% -> 0.3%) OR doubling from baseline, whichever is more sensitive -> immediate rollback.
- Cache regression: cache_hit_rate drop > 5 percentage points over 6h -> pause and investigate.

Secondary / analysis metrics (longer-window, 24h+):
- Cost-per-inference median and tail, per-tenant and per-model variant.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 trends.
- Throughput (requests/sec) and batch-size distribution.
- Quality regressions against small blackbox evals: token-level perplexity and a small prompt set score. We will not gate auto-rollback on these (too noisy) but use them for roll-to-production decisions.

Statistical approach:
- Power target: 80% power to detect a 5% improvement in unit cost at alpha=0.05. Use pre-rollout sample-size calc to estimate time-to-power at each canary size.
- Short-window automated checks use deterministic thresholds (not hypothesis tests) for rapid safety.
- Final experiment evaluation uses difference-in-differences with bootstrap confidence intervals per-tenant and a hierarchical model to surface outlier tenants that benefit/hurt.

Rollout automation plan:
- Stages: dry-run (simulated metric calc on production traffic snapshot), canary-1 (1% steady-state sample), canary-2 (5%), canary-3 (20%), full.
- Minimum dwell time per stage: configurable (default 2h at 1%/5%, 12h at 20%).
- Automated rollback triggers evaluate consecutive violation windows (configurable, default 2).
- Manual override: owners can force-advance or pause; when paused a mandatory incident VR (owner + eng on-call) is notified.
- All rollouts produce an immutable audit log entry with metrics snapshot and diff.

Dashboards and alerts:
- Dashboard template (Console):
  - Top row: global smoke metrics (unit cost delta, latency p95 delta, error rate delta, cache_hit_rate delta) with current window and sparkline.
  - Middle: cohort comparison panels (control vs variant) for cost by model and tenant top-20 by traffic.
  - Bottom: rollouts timeline + recent audit entries, and per-tenant small-multiple panels.
  - Link-outs: GitHub PR, Confluence PRD, evaluation harness run.
- Alerting rules:
  - PagerDuty critical: error rate spike trigger or latency spike as defined above.
  - PagerDuty high: cost regression > 12% sustained for 6h.
  - Slack notify: canary stage transitions and when statistical significance is reached.

Data retention & privacy:
- Per-request telemetry retained for 30 days in high-cardinality store, aggregated metrics retained 90 days. Tenant identifiers in dashboards masked for public links.

Operational playbook (short):
- On auto-rollback: system creates rollback PR (or auto-applies a safe fallback variant) and notifies on-call + owners with reason + metric snapshots.
- Owner responsibilities: run quick replay/trace for any anomalous request, consult model quality dashboard, review GC/infra metrics.
- Postmortem: mandatory for any rollback where customer_impact >= medium; include metric diffs and timeline.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize exact sampling method for 1% canary (random request hashing vs tenant-based routing to avoid splitting small tenants).
- Decide if cache_ttl buckets need per-tenant overrides in rollout.
- Power calculation automation: should the rollout automation surface estimated time-to-power per canary size? (proposal: yes).

Acceptance criteria:
- Experiment telemetry tags are emitted for control/variant on production requests.
- Automatic canary rollout automation implemented with 1/5/20/100 stages and configurable dwell times.
- Console dashboard template created and accessible to on-call and PM.
- Alert rules implemented and tested in staging with simulated metric violations.
- Automated rollback path tested end-to-end (simulation + small live canary) and triggers produce audit logs and notifications.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Control/variant tagging present on production requests and visible in metrics.
2) Canary automation supports stage progression and auto-rollback based on smoke thresholds.
3) Dashboard template with required panels exists in Console and can be cloned per experiment.
4) PagerDuty + Slack alerts fire correctly on simulated violations in staging.
5) Post-rollback audit entry includes metric snapshots and the rollback reason.
